test_title: PYST 19: SSC CGL - English (Held On : 21 April 2022 Shift 1)
subject: english
question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in active voice.

Rishabh was declared fit to play the next match.

options.text: Rishabh declared them fit to play the next match.
They had declared Rishabh fit to play the next match.
They will declare Rishabh fit to play the next match.
They declared Rishabh fit to play the next match.

solution:
The correct answer is** 'They declared Rishabh fit to play the next match.'**

**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence is in **passive voice.** As per the question we have to change it into** active voice.**
 
• The structure of the given sentence is as follows:
 
 
• **Subject (objective case) + was + past participle + by Object (subjective case) (Passive voice) + adjunct**
 
• **Subject + past participle + Object (Active voice) + adjunct**
 
 
 
• Example: 
 
 
• *A large house was built by her.(Passive voice)*
 
• *She built a large house. (Active voice)*
 
 
 
• The **subject **of the given sentence is ‘Rishabh’.
 
• The object of the given subject is ‘they’.
 
• The subject will be put in place of the object and the object will be put in place of the subject. 
 
• **"was declared"** will be changed to "**declared"**.
 
• **Adjunct **is a word or phrase that constitutes an optional element or is considered of secondary importance in a sentence
 
 
• In the given sentence, *to play the next match. *is the **adjunct. **
 
 
 
• Correct sentence - **They declared Rishabh fit to play the next match.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• We do not use an object in the passive sentences wherein in active sentences the subject is unknown or is not required to be written i.e. it is understood from the very sentence like someone, somebody, nobody, people etc.
